input.summary: Amara meets UCL’s Nigerian upper-second equivalency and has a relevant Physics degree, but the supplied record does not establish the programme’s normal doctoral prerequisite: a relevant Master’s/equivalent. sections.title: Current official programme requirements
sections.body: For 2026–27 entry, UCL Physics and Astronomy MPhil/PhD requires either: (1) a minimum upper-second UK integrated Master’s (MSci/MPhys) in a relevant discipline; (2) an undergraduate degree followed by an MSc in a relevant discipline; or (3) an equivalent overseas qualification. UCL’s course page says applicants are generally expected to have the equivalent of a good UK Master’s and that the programme will not accept candidates qualified only to Bachelor’s level. It separately states that an upper-second or first Bachelor’s/equivalent may be considered only in special circumstances. The programme identifies High Energy Particle Physics as a research group, which is substantively aligned with Amara’s stated particle-detector interests. citeturn0search0turn1search3

sections.title: Academic and subject comparison
sections.body: Verified from the supplied transcript: Amara holds a BSc Physics from the University of Lagos, completed June 14, 2024 and conferred July 31, 2024, with a 4.62/5.00 CGPA and relevant Quantum Mechanics, Electrodynamics, Statistical Mechanics, Mathematical Methods, Nuclear and Particle Physics, and Computational Physics courses. UCL’s current Nigeria equivalency guidance gives 3.75/5.0 as the minimum benchmark for a UK upper-second equivalent, so the 4.62/5.00 result exceeds that published benchmark. Physics is plainly a relevant subject for the Physics and Astronomy programme. This establishes a strong Bachelor’s-level academic and subject match, but it does not substitute for the programme’s normal Master’s-level prerequisite. citeturn1search1

sections.title: Determination
sections.body: Standard-route prerequisite: NOT SATISFIED / NOT VERIFIED. The materials show no MSc, MPhys, MSci, or other postgraduate qualification. Special-circumstances route: POSSIBLE BUT NOT VERIFIABLE from the available materials; UCL does not define the special circumstances on the programme page, so admission would remain discretionary and should not be represented as eligibility. CERN OpenLab research employment, the detector project, programming skills, and publication submission strengthen academic fit but are not stated by UCL as replacements for the required postgraduate qualification.

sections.title: Other consequential requirements and gaps
sections.body: English: the programme requires UCL English Level 1. For a Nigerian citizen, the supplied materials do not contain an accepted recent test result or other evidence meeting that requirement; UCL’s current Level 1 IELTS benchmark is 6.5 overall with at least 6.0 in each component, with equivalent routes also available. The page states that two references are required; the likely strongest documented referees are Professor Ifeanyi Eze and Dr Sofia Marin, but no submitted references are evidenced. UCL says applicants should generally identify and contact potential supervisors before applying. The programme accepts applications on a rolling basis, ordinarily at least three months before the preferred start date; no specific application deadline is verified from the supplied materials. citeturn1search0turn0search0

sections.title: What cannot be verified
sections.body: Cannot verify: (a) any Master’s-level qualification or equivalent postgraduate study; (b) whether UCL would accept Amara under its undefined special-circumstances exception; (c) English-language compliance; (d) supervisor contact or support; (e) whether a particular funded studentship is available or whether full tuition plus stipend would be secured. The programme page lists the 2026/27 China Scholarship Council–UCL Joint Research Scholarship as closed, but that does not determine eligibility for other funding routes. citeturn0search0

follow_ups: Obtain confirmation of any postgraduate qualification or ask UCL Graduate Admissions whether the Bachelor’s-only special-circumstances exception could apply.
Provide an accepted English-language result or documented basis for exemption.
Identify and contact a suitable UCL High Energy Physics supervisor before relying on this programme.
